_comment: Tool-name provenance. The two conditions differ ONLY in --tools and -e; model,
system prompt, task prompt and work dir are identical, so any difference in tokens
or pass rate is attributable to the tool set.
THE EIGHT TOOL NAMES, read verbatim from the `TOOLS` array in omp-extension/mm.ts,
in source order:
mm_check, mm_symbol, mm_refs, mm_type, mm_slice, mm_packet, mm_system, mm_verify
There is no `mm_explain`. Diagnostics are `mm_check`, which maps to the daemon verb
`mm.diagnostics`; the CLI surfaces that verb to humans as `explain`. The extension
renamed it, so the tool is `mm_check`.
HOW --tools BEHAVES, measured on the installed omp v18.4.3 rather than assumed.
Three cases were run directly:
A. extension registers mm_check, --tools=read,mm_check   -> works, tool callable
B. extension registers mm_check, --tools=read             -> works, tool STILL
callable: extension-registered tools are force-included in the active set
C. extension registers only mm_check, --tools=read,mm_slice -> hard startup error,
'Unknown tool in --tools: mm_slice', listing mm_check under registered tools
So naming the mm_* tools in --tools is NOT a no-op on this version: it is a load-time
ASSERTION. Case C is the reason the semantic list keeps them. If the extension fails
to load, the run dies immediately instead of silently continuing with only the four
built-ins, which would be a semantic condition that quietly measures the baseline.
Note this contradicts omp://custom-tools.md ('--tools currently validates only
built-in tool names'); the observed v18.4.3 behaviour above is what the harness
actually depends on, and case C is the regression test for it.
The semantic extension is .harness/loader/mm-ext.ts, not omp-extension/mm.ts itself.
The library has no default export, and omp loads an extension by taking the module
or module.default as a factory, so `-e omp-extension/mm.ts` fails to load. The
loader is the OMP-loadable adapter: it default-exports the factory, spawns mmd
lazily per cwd, and forwards calls through the library's own MmExtension so the
tool-name-to-verb mapping stays owned by the library. It sits outside every run's
work/ directory so the agent under test cannot edit the tool it is measured on.
